Four high-criticality risk items have OQ test coverage but no PQ coverage, where PQ evidence is expected. They come from two underlying performance requirements.

**Method**
- High criticality means `risk_class = 'HIGH'`. I did not re-derive it from RPN.
- PQ is expected for requirements with `req_category = 'PERFORMANCE'` on EQUIPMENT systems.
- A risk is linked to a requirement either through an FRA row (ASSESSES) or through a pFMEA row (MITIGATED_BY).
- Coverage follows the verification path. A test case verifies the requirement directly, or through its FS, CS or DS children. I then looked at the protocol type of each test case (OQ or PQ).

**Result**

| Risk (pFMEA) | Risk (FRA) | Requirement | System | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FM-02, selection program parameters (HIGH) | FRA-014 | URS-PRDG-002 (locked CD4/CD8 enrichment program, purity ≥90% CD3+) | SYS-PRDG | Only TC-OQ-PRDG-02 (OQ-PRDG-01, scripted). No PQ test case. |
| FM-13, freeze profile (HIGH) | FRA-020 | URS-CRF-001 (CRF-P01 freeze profile within ±2 °C with a representative load) | SYS-CRF | Only TC-OQ-CRF-01 (OQ-CRF-01, scripted). No PQ test case. |

- Other high-criticality risks on equipment performance requirements do have PQ coverage. These are FRA-001 and FM-09 (INC-001), FRA-008 and FM-07 (ULT-001), FRA-013 and FM-03 (PRDG-001), and FRA-019 (LOVO-002).
- High risks on ALARM requirements on equipment systems have OQ only. These are FRA-003, FRA-004 and FRA-009. They are excluded because alarm requirements are fully verified at OQ, so PQ is not expected.
- High risks on the EMS, LIMS and EBR systems are excluded because they are computerized systems, so PQ does not apply.

The four risk IDs in the answer are FM-02, FM-13, FRA-014 and FRA-020. If you only want the process FMEA, that is FM-02 and FM-13. If you only want the functional risk assessment rows, it is FRA-014 and FRA-020.
